hypotheses.description: The two products are spatially misaligned (e.g., a shift or rotation) causing low agreement despite both being valid.
One product has a systematic bias (e.g., offset or scaling) relative to the other, reducing agreement without spatial misalignment.
The products are generated by different algorithms or processing chains that legitimately produce different spatial patterns, so the low agreement is scientifically valid.
One or both products contain corrupted or erroneous pixel values (e.g., from sensor artifacts) that are not flagged as invalid, lowering agreement.

selected_experiment.expected_evidence: Measure evidence that distinguishes the target hypotheses.
